text:
Sam H.: hey — running into a weird parity bug between node and python SDKs for embeddings+rerank. sample app sends a batch of 6 queries but rerank output is 5 vectors for node and 6 for python :confused:

Priya K.: can you paste the request payload (sanitized) + response from both SDKs? quick glance: sounds like ordering/dup drop or retry de-dupe.

Sam H.: yup. node request (shortened):
```json
{
  "model": "embed-small-v1",
  "input": ["q1","q2","q3","q4","q5","q6"],
  "batch_helper": {"enabled": true, "max_batch_size": 8}
}
```
node response (shape):
```json
{
  "data": [/* 5 items only */],
  "meta": {"request_id": "abc123", "sdk": "node"}
}
```
python request is identical but response has 6 items.

Diego R.: fwiw we had an auth edge where a 401 triggers a retry that replays a sub-batch without original ids, then the batching helper collapses duplicates. could be related. did you see any 401 or 429 in the logs? :eyes: 

Sam H.: no obvious 401 in the app logs. i copied the raw HTTP sequence from the node SDK:
```
POST /v1/embeddings 200 OK (first chunk)
POST /v1/embeddings 200 OK (second chunk)
POST /v1/embeddings 500 Internal (third chunk) -> SDK retries sub-batch -> 200 OK
```
looks like retry occurred for the last sub-batch.

Maya L.: aha. the batching helper in node merges back responses using index positions; if a retry returns a shorter array (server trimmed duplicates) we can accidentally drop indices. python helper uses explicit id tags and reorders by original id, so it's resilient.

Priya K.: Maya — is that the known "index-merge on concat" behavior in the node helper? iirc there was a change where we avoided adding ids for perf.

Maya L.: yes — tradeoff was fewer bytes over the wire. but it assumed server always returns same-length arrays per sub-batch. with retry/replay semantics that's unsafe.

Sam H.: ok that explains parity. two follow-ups: 1) any short-term workaround for node users? 2) is there a server-side change we can push to avoid dropping duplicates on retries?

Alex Z.: short-term: disable batching helper in node (set batch_helper.enabled=false) or set helper to tag items with client_id: true. example:
```js
await client.embeddings.create({
  model: 'embed-small-v1',
  input: queries,
  batch_helper: {enabled: true, tag_ids: true}
})
```
this forces per-item ids so replays can be reconciled.

Priya K.: long-term: i'll open a devx ticket to change default node helper to include lightweight ids when retry is enabled. also logging improvement: include sub-batch id in telemetry so we can trace replayed chunks.

devx-bot: Created issue DEVEX-4321: "node batching helper: add id tagging when retryable requests enabled" — https://rwd.in/DEVEX-4321 :white_check_mark:

Sam H.: second issue: node response format currently returns embeddings array but doesn't include per-item metadata (original_input, client_id). python response includes a parallel metadata array. that makes parity hard for downstream rerank mapper. can we standardize to always include per-item meta?

Maya L.: agreed — we should have a stable response contract: for batched endpoints we return an array of objects [{embedding: [...], input: "...", client_id: "..."}] rather than two separate arrays. breaking change though.

Alex Z.: proposed migration path: opt-in response_shape=object_items header for one release; then after 2 releases flip default and keep compatibility flag for older SDKs. update docs + SDKs simultaneously.

Diego R.: note: server currently supports `include_input` query param for debug; we can use that as a stopgap to return original_input in the payload so node can map. less efficient but fast to test.

Sam H.: i'll try include_input=true and tag_ids=true and report back. thanks all.

Priya K.: thx — file a short reproduction snippet and paste it into DEVEX-4321 so eng can reproduce load+retry pattern.

Sam H.: will do. reproduction gist in 10m. :thumbsup:
